title: Windows and Doors Rebates in Burlington 2026: $100 Per Opening and Lake-Effect Winters
desc: Burlington window and door rebates for 2026: $100 per rough opening under Home Renovation Savings, with 47% of homes built before 1981.
h1: Windows and Doors Rebates in Burlington
lead: Burlington has 73,180 households and 75% own. 47% live in homes built before 1981, which puts it in the middle of our Ontario cities for housing age.
cards_heading: What the Home Renovation Savings program pays for windows and doors in Burlington
cards_intro: We re-read the program's page and its eligibility requirements on October 3, 2026. Windows and doors are paid only inside the assessment stream, so every amount here comes with an assessment and at least two upgrades.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: One payment per opening in an outside wall, not per unit. A bay window with three panes in one opening earns $100.

cards.title: Smallest qualifying job
cards.note: Three window openings, or one door, sliding door or skylight opening, count as one qualified measure. Two windows alone earn nothing.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: Covers the cost of the first and the follow-up assessment once the program is completed.

cards.title: Three or more upgrades
cards.note: Windows count as one upgrade. Insulation, air sealing and a heat pump water heater are the others in this stream.

cards.title: Program cap
cards.note: $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $5,000 for homes heated by Enbridge gas.

after_cards: The program is run by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy. Post-audits must be scheduled by November 30, 2026 and completed by December 31, 2026, or within 180 days of your first assessment, whichever comes first.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 19,345 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Burlington. 50% of households live in detached houses and 73% in an eligible house type. 4.1% report needing major repairs. Apartments in buildings of five or more storeys account for 18% of households and are outside the program.

Burlington's January average low is -7.2°C and the record low from 2015 to 2024 was -26.2°C. That is milder than Ottawa or Barrie. The rebate does not depend on climate, but replacement windows should be an ENERGY STAR certified model suited to your climate zone, so ask the supplier to show the certified rating.

The window rebate is not available alone. It needs at least two qualifying measures in the assessment stream. If your main goal is a heat pump, the separate stream pays up to $7,500 for a cold-climate air-source model without an audit, so the audit bundle is a separate decision.

The ENERGY STAR labels have to stay on the new windows and doors until after the post-audit. They are easy to peel off during installation or cleaning. Tell whoever works on the house to leave them, and take photos of each label as soon as the windows go in.

Your total rebate under the assessment stream is capped at $5,000 for a home heated by Enbridge gas and $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood, judged at the time of the audits. A Burlington house that burns gas and plans a heat pump later should read the heat pump rules too, since the heat pump stream has its own requirements and the two can be done by the same household at different times.
claim_steps: Confirm you own the home, it has been occupied for six months and it is one of the eligible house types.
Book the first home energy assessment with a registered energy advisor before any work starts.
Choose at least one more upgrade to pair with the windows, and get quotes that count rough openings the way the program does.
Ask the supplier to show the ENERGY STAR rating for your climate zone.
Have a professional install complete windows or doors with frames, keep the ENERGY STAR labels on until the follow-up assessment, and book it.
faq: Yes. The January average low is -7.2 degrees Celsius against -13.2 in Ottawa.
Can I claim windows without other upgrades?
No. You need at least two qualifying measures.
The advisor checks them at the post-audit.
Is there a separate heat pump rebate?
Yes, up to $7,500 for a cold-climate air-source heat pump without an audit.
